c.tagline: Gateway city beneath the near-perfect cone of Mayon Volcano

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis are scarce; tricycles (motorcycle sidecars) are the main short-distance transport with fixed or lightly negotiated fares, and Grab is available for point-to-point city rides.

emergency.note: 911 is the Philippines' nationwide emergency hotline covering police, fire, and medical services.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: No no-go districts in the city itself; avoid remote inland areas of Bicol where NPA rebel activity is occasionally reported.
Pickpockets at the public market and bus terminals, and always check Mayon Volcano alert levels before booking hikes or ATV tours.

hood_desc: The modern commercial heart of Legazpi, built up after WWII around Peñaranda Park, with government offices, malls, and the city's main hotels. It's the most convenient base for exploring the rest of the city, with Mayon Volcano views on clear days.

The original town center dating to Spanish colonial times, centered on the 18th-century Sto. Domingo de Guzman Church and a scattering of ancestral houses. It has a quieter, more historic feel than the newer port area a few kilometers away.

A waterfront leisure complex built on a former pier, with a boardwalk, shops, restaurants, and a small amusement park facing Legazpi Bay with Mayon Volcano as backdrop. Popular for sunset views and weekend strolls.

A bayside barangay at the foot of Lignon Hill Nature Park, where a short hike or shuttle ride leads to sweeping panoramic views of Mayon Volcano and the city. Calmer and more residential than downtown.
A road lined with restaurants, cafes, and bars that has become Legazpi's go-to strip for evening dining and casual nightlife, popular for trying Bicol's famously spicy, coconut-milk-heavy cuisine.

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water, as in most provincial Philippine cities.

transit.map: No official app; jeepney routes are known locally by destination barangay
transit.note: Tricycles are the easiest way to get around the city; jeepneys serve fixed routes cheaply; Grab is available for app-based rides.

air: Bicol International Airport (LGP) - direct flights from Manila and Cebu
train: No functioning long-distance passenger rail currently serves the Bicol region
bus: Overnight buses connect to Manila (9-12 hr) and other Bicol/Luzon cities
ferry: Limited inter-island connections via nearby Tabaco and Matnog ports (e.g., to Masbate, Samar)

tip.s: not obligatory but increasingly expected in tourism
tip.r: A 10% tip in restaurants is appreciated (some already add a service charge); rounding up for tricycles/taxis and small tips for tour guides and hotel staff are customary.
